meta_description: Compare Anime Expeditions Stat Potential grades by Damage, SPA, Range, and single-stat chance, then plan rerolls and Stat Locks.
intro_md: Stat Potential gives each unit separate grades for Damage, SPA, and Range. A shiny letter is only half the story: the percentage band tells you how much that particular stat actually changes.
description_md:
## Reading Damage, SPA, and Range rolls

Damage and Range are simple: a positive percentage raises the stat, while a negative percentage lowers it. SPA means seconds per attack, so it works in the opposite direction. Negative SPA shortens the wait between attacks and makes the unit attack faster. Positive SPA makes the wait longer, which is the kind of plus sign nobody invited.

Each stat rolls independently. The chance shown for a grade applies to one Damage, SPA, or Range roll, not to the chance of landing that grade on all three stats at once. A unit can therefore have a strong Damage grade, a weaker Range grade, and a completely different SPA result.

## Deciding when to reroll

Judge the unit by what its kit needs, not by one letter alone. Damage is broadly useful, Range matters more when placement or map coverage is tight, and faster SPA can be especially valuable for units that benefit from attacking more often.

A mixed result can still be worth using while reroll materials are limited. The lower grades may add some Damage while slowing SPA or cutting Range, so check every stat before deciding that one positive number has saved the roll.

## Using Stat Locks

A Stat Lock protects a result you want to keep while you reroll the remaining stats. This is useful when one stat already has a rare or build-defining grade, but spending locks on an ordinary result can leave you short when a much better roll appears later.

Set a stopping point before chasing the rarest grade. A balanced set of useful rolls can improve a unit now, while an endless hunt for matching top grades can turn reroll items into very expensive confetti.
how_it_works_md: Quality gives a quick read on the grade. Single-stat chance is the chance for one independently rolled stat, while Damage, SPA, and Range show the exact percentage band that grade can produce.

faq_json.q: Is negative SPA good in Anime Expeditions?
faq_json.a: Yes. SPA is the time between attacks, so a negative SPA percentage shortens that time and makes the unit attack faster. A positive SPA percentage slows the unit down.

faq_json.q: Does the grade chance apply to all unit stats together?
faq_json.a: No. The chance applies to one stat roll. Damage, SPA, and Range roll independently, so each can land on a different grade.

faq_json.q: What does a Stat Lock do?
faq_json.a: A Stat Lock keeps a chosen stat result while the other stats are rerolled. It helps protect a strong roll while you work on weaker ones.

faq_json.q: Should I lock every positive stat roll?
faq_json.a: Usually not. Save locks for results that are rare or important to that unit's build, especially when the other stats still need work.

faq_json.q: Why can a lower grade still increase Damage?
faq_json.a: The grade bands do not affect every stat in the same direction. Some lower grades can give a small Damage increase while also adding slower SPA and reduced Range.

faq_json.q: Do I need matching grades on Damage, SPA, and Range?
faq_json.a: No. A useful set of rolls depends on the unit and your resources. Strong results in the stats that matter most can be a sensible stopping point even when the letters do not match.

wiki_md: Stat Potential rolls Damage, SPA, and Range separately for each unit. Damage and Range prefer positive percentages, while SPA prefers a negative percentage because it shortens the time between attacks. Stat Locks preserve a strong result while you reroll weaker stats, making the choice of what to keep part of the upgrade plan.
